Its promise is immense - to decarbonize heavy industry, enable green industrialization, create inclusive jobs, and strengthen energy security - yet its trajectory remains uncertain. How can green hydrogen truly become a development pathway?
 
The task for countries is to navigate this uncertainty wisely: aligning investments with national priorities that integrate hydrogen into energy and industrial strategies which build domestic value chains, expand energy access, develop skills and jobs, and protect land, water, and biodiversity - rather than locking into extractive models.
 
Green hydrogen must serve sustainable development, not just markets. People must be at the center, with local value chains that create jobs and new industries. A priority of needs of the Planet must guide the use and preservation of water and land for long-term resilience. And Prosperity should be shared - with green hydrogen fueling industrialization, enhancing energy security, and decarbonizing growth.
 
Our new policy paper by UNDP and TIDE Centre, University of Oxford, Navigating the Currents of Green Hydrogen: Towards a Human Development-Centred Framework, introduces this 3P approach - People, Planet, and Prosperity - to help countries steer green hydrogen at the right speed, time, and direction 👉 bit.ly/Green-H2
